subject: Driver liveness: dead mid-way / awaiting takeover / taken over are told apart, and `actl heartbeat --reconcile` puts tickets, events, land lock and worktree debris back to the facts
objective: After a container restart (or any killed auto-fix / land / review / main session), one command reports every unmatched start as alive / dead-awaiting-takeover / taken-over / unknown by reading /proc and boot_id (never a signal), and `--reconcile` does what main did by hand 4+ times on 2026-10-21..26: closes the dead round's events and sessions.json rows, saves the worktree's uncommitted work to reports/t<n>/<run_id>/wip-round<r>-died.diff and leaves the worktree clean, writes the dead round's cost row, puts the ticket back to Ready, removes a dead land's lock and debris, and emits the closer events so heartbeat is quiet afterwards. No daemon (#120 cancelled): facts are read at session start and on demand.
acceptance: A1 Start events carry the driver: `ticket.attempt.start` and `agent.start` (auto-fix.sh, review.sh, consolidate-memory.sh, new-session.sh dispatch), `land.start` (land.sh), `session.start` (session-hook.sh / new-session.sh main) get kv `driver_pid=<pid of the emitting driver, not of event.py>` and `boot_id=<content of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id>`. The land lock holder line gets `boot_id=` next to `pid=`. Rows written before this ticket (no kv) are still read: they fall back to the lease rule and are reported as `unknown`, never `alive`.

A2 `actl heartbeat` (read-only, unchanged exit codes 0/1/2, same `heartbeat:   ` line prefix that new-session.sh's awk filters) reports every unmatched start with one verdict word: `alive` (driver_pid present in /proc and boot_id equal to the current one - printed even past the lease, exit code contribution 0), `dead` (pid gone or boot differs) with sub-state `awaiting-takeover` (no later start for the same key, H2) or `taken-over by <run_id/attempt/stamp>`, or `unknown (no driver recorded; lease rule)`. Verdicts are computed by ONE liveness implementation shared with scripts/schedule.py `gone()` (moved to a module both import; a second copy is an objection) and read only /proc - no signal of any kind.

A3 `actl heartbeat --reconcile` acts only on `dead` + `awaiting-takeover`; `alive`, `taken-over` and `unknown` rows are printed and left alone (`unknown` tells the human what to check). It is idempotent: a second run reports 'nothing to reconcile' and writes no event, no file, no ticket change.

A4 Dead worker / verifier round r of run R for ticket n: (i) if the ticket worktree has uncommitted or untracked changes, their diff (H3) is written to reports/t<n>/<R>/wip-round<r>-died.diff and the worktree is then clean (`git status --porcelain` empty; branch head untouched; commits made before death stay); an empty diff writes no file; (ii) reports/t<n>/<R>/worker.pid (and the verifier's) removed; (iii) sessions.json rows for that run -> state=closed, why=driver-died, closed_at; (iv) events `agent.failed` (role, round, run_id, kv reason=driver-died) for each open agent row and `ticket.attempt.failed attempt=r reason=driver-died`; (v) one cost row per dead agent via `ticket.py cost <n> --role <role> --round r --from-envelope <that round's log> --outcome error --note driver-died --run-id R` (with #124 landed the tokens come from the transcript; without it the row is nulls with the existing reason - this ticket does not parse logs); (vi) ticket state Running -> Ready (so the scheduler frontier / `actl schedule run` / auto-fix can re-dispatch); InReview stays InReview (a dead reviewer only gets `agent.failed` + `review.missing`); Blocked / Done / Cancelled are never changed; (vii) the dead round's dispatch / log / result files are kept where they are - the next round of the same run must not overwrite them: auto-fix.sh names a re-dispatched round's files with a `-r2` style suffix or mints a new run_id (worker's choice, written in EVIDENCE); the test asserts the dead round's worker log still exists byte-identical after the next round ran.

A5 Dead land (land.start with stamp S, no land.pass/fail/refused for S, holder pid gone or boot differs): .land.lock removed, `land.fail stamp=S stage=died main_before=<holder's or event's main_before if recorded> note=driver-died` emitted so heartbeat pairs it, the land/<S> worktree and branch removed. A land whose stamp already has a terminal event (red kept on purpose, conflict) is NOT touched - still listed as debris as today. A live holder (pid in /proc, same boot) is named and nothing is removed. land.sh `take_lock` itself takes over a lock whose holder is dead by the same shared rule (prints 'stale lock pid X taken over'), instead of refusing and asking a human.

A6 Dead main session (session.start role=main, driver_pid gone or boot differs): `session.end` with kv reason=driver-died is emitted; a session with no driver_pid (pre-A1 rows) stays `unknown` and is not ended.

A7 Dead scheduler run (reports/schedule/state.json stop=null, pid gone/boot differs): heartbeat prints it as `dead awaiting-takeover` with the resume hint `actl schedule run` and `--reconcile` does NOT touch state.json or the schedule lock (schedule.py already resumes and takes over its own stale lock, #119 A6/A11); its orphan auto-fix children are reconciled by A4 only when they are dead themselves.

A8 Output for humans: each reconciled item prints one line `heartbeat: reconciled <what> -> <done>`; the summary is also appended to reports/heartbeat/<timestamp>.log (not a page: reconcile is main's own action, D-032 pages are for decisions); no `decision` inbox page is written by reconcile.
A9 No new line matching hard_block.patterns (os\.kill, killpg, pkill, `kill -`) in tests/ or verify/; liveness code outside tests contains no signal call either (grep in the verifier case).

A10 docs: docs/WORKFLOW.md gets a short section 'A driver died' (what heartbeat reports, what --reconcile does, what it never does) and docs/SESSION-START.md's main-role step says `actl heartbeat` then `--reconcile` when it reports dead rows; tickets/SCHEMA.md: nothing new on the ticket (no sessions registry on the ticket, no new fields).
in_scope: Driver pid + boot_id on start events and the land lock; shared liveness module; heartbeat verdicts; `actl heartbeat --reconcile` for dead worker/verifier rounds, dead land, dead reviewer, dead main session; docs.
out_of_scope: No daemon / controller (#120 cancelled). No automatic re-dispatch (the scheduler / main does that from Ready). No resume of the dead agent's session (D-067: every round is a new agent). No sessions.json schema change beyond state/why/closed_at. No token parsing (#124). No change to the repair budget (#125). docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md (hard_block).
outline: Rewritten 2026-10-26 per D-076 (old draft: sessions registry schema v2, claims, slots, #120 Controller - all dropped; #120/#123 cancelled, #119 schedule landed). Verified by reading (not run): heartbeat.sh = lease-only + land debris; schedule.py has pid+boot_id liveness for its own children (gone(), Lock.take, orphan()); event.py pid = emitter pid; land.sh take_lock refuses on any existing lock; auto-fix run_agent writes <round dir>/worker.pid, removed on return; sessions.json rows open/closed via session_open/session_close; events: 1 session.start role=main, 0 session.end. Evidence of the manual loop: reports/t{155,159,169}/wip-round1-timeout.diff, reports/t162/wip-round2-restart.diff. Files that will move: scripts/heartbeat.sh (+ maybe scripts/heartbeat.py), scripts/schedule.py (import shared gone()), scripts/event.py (none required), scripts/auto-fix.sh (ev kv on start events; round-file naming on re-dispatch), scripts/land.sh (holder boot_id, take over dead lock, land.start kv), scripts/review.sh, scripts/consolidate-memory.sh, scripts/new-session.sh, scripts/session-hook.sh ($PPID best effort), tests/test_heartbeat.py, tests/test_schedule.py (A6 stale holder test must keep passing), tests/test_land.py, tests/test_auto_fix.py, tests/test_session_hook.py, tests/test_new_session.py (awk filter of heartbeat lines), docs/WORKFLOW.md, docs/SESSION-START.md. Pinned old behaviour checked: tests/test_heartbeat.py lease wording and land-debris listing; tests/test_schedule.py test_a6_stale_holder_is_taken_over, test_a11_* (resume). needs_verifier=true: cross-process liveness and crash boundaries need independent cases. interface_fixed=true: verdict words, kv names, file names and the CLI flag are fixed above, so the verifier starts in parallel. complexity=complex. Overlap with #125: both edit scripts/auto-fix.sh (different sections: event kv / re-dispatch file naming here, round budget + diagnosis dispatch there) - land in order #124, #117, #125. Relation to #124: A4(v) calls ticket.py cost on the dead round's log; tokens appear only once #124 landed - not a dependency.
feature: agent-control: driver liveness and reconcile after a crash
test_plan:
All tests in tests/ against a throwaway control root (tests/control_harness.py); clear AC_ROOT / AC_TICKETS_DIR / AC_CONTROL_DIR; no real LLM; expected values come from the fixture, not from the code under test.
T1 (unit, verdicts; tests/test_heartbeat.py) Fixture events: (a) ticket.attempt.start with driver_pid=<a pid the test proved absent: spawn `true` and wait for it> and boot_id=<current boot read by the test> -> line contains `dead awaiting-takeover`; exit code 1. (b) driver_pid=<pid of a `sleep 300` child the test spawned> same boot, ts 3 h old (past lease 7200) -> `alive`, exit code 0 when nothing else is open. (c) driver_pid=1 (alive) with boot_id=`00000000-dead` -> `dead`. (d) as (a) plus a later ticket.attempt.start attempt+1 for the same ticket -> `dead taken-over by attempt 2`; a later start for ANOTHER ticket -> still `awaiting-takeover`. (e) a row without driver_pid 3 h old -> `unknown` and the existing lease wording (existing tests test_a_session_past_its_lease_* and test_two_lines_running_at_once_* unchanged and green). (f) land.start stamp S with dead driver and no terminal event -> `dead awaiting-takeover`; with a land.fail for S -> not listed as open (existing test_a_refused_land_counts_as_come_back).
T2 (integration, reconcile worker round; tests/test_heartbeat.py or a new tests/test_reconcile.py) Build: ticket n Running, branch t<n> worktree with one commit after base, one modified tracked file, one untracked file, reports/t<n>/<R>/worker.pid, sessions.json worker row open, events attempt.start + agent.start with a dead driver, a worker-round1.log (any text). Before the call the test computes expected diff = `git add -N . && git diff HEAD` output. After `actl heartbeat --reconcile`: wip-round1-died.diff == expected; porcelain empty; branch head unchanged; worker.pid gone; sessions row closed/why=driver-died; events attempt.failed reason=driver-died and agent.failed reason=driver-died present exactly once; ticket state Ready, state_version +1; one cost row role=worker round=1 outcome=error note contains driver-died run_id=R; no inbox page written; second run -> 'nothing to reconcile', event count unchanged.
T3 (integration, land) .land.lock/holder `pid=<absent> boot_id=<current>` + land.start stamp S + land/<S> worktree and branch -> after reconcile: lock dir gone, land.fail stamp=S stage=died present, worktree and branch gone. Variant: stamp S has land.fail already -> worktree kept, lock untouched. Variant: holder pid = live sleep child -> nothing removed, line says `alive`. land.sh: with a dead holder, `sh scripts/land.sh t<n>` proceeds and prints the takeover line (tests/test_land.py).
T4 (integration, main session) session.start role=main driver_pid=<absent> -> session.end reason=driver-died emitted; without driver_pid -> no session.end.
T5 (events carry the driver) auto-fix harness round 1 (tests/test_auto_fix.py): ticket.attempt.start and agent.start rows have driver_pid == the auto-fix.sh pid (the harness reads it from the emitted row and checks it is not event.py's: it differs between the two rows' `pid` field and equals across them) and boot_id == current; land.start in tests/test_land.py likewise; holder line has boot_id=.
T6 (next round does not overwrite) after T2, run auto-fix round 2 in the harness: the dead round's worker-round1.log is byte-identical afterwards.
T7 (hard_block) grep of the branch diff's added lines in tests/ and verify/ for hard_block.patterns = 0 hits (gate preflight does this; the verifier also asserts no `os.kill(`/`killpg(` in the liveness module).
Mutations (worker runs, states which test goes red): M1 drop the boot_id comparison in gone() -> T1(c) red. M2 reconcile treats `taken-over` like `awaiting-takeover` -> T1(d)/T2 variant red (the newer attempt would get a failed event). M3 write the wip diff but skip cleaning -> T2 red (porcelain not empty). M4 remove the land worktree regardless of a terminal event -> T3 variant red. M5 emit driver_pid from event.py's os.getpid() -> T5 red. Not measured by the opener (read-only opening); the worker hands in red/green evidence.
problem: Evidence: reports/t162/wip-round2-restart.diff, reports/t155|t159|t169/wip-round1-timeout.diff (all hand-made by main), HANDOFF 2026-10-22 ('container restarted 3 times, background work killed') and 2026-10-26 ('long runs must be setsid nohup; the container restarts'). What a killed driver leaves behind today: ticket Running with nobody on it; `ticket.attempt.start` / `agent.start` / `land.start` with no closer; reports/t<n>/<run>/worker.pid (removed only on return, auto-fix.sh run_agent); reports/t<n>/sessions.json rows state=open; the worktree with uncommitted work; .land.lock/holder (pid only, no boot id; land.sh take_lock refuses and tells a human to rm -rf); land/<stamp> worktree + branch. heartbeat.sh can only say 'lease expired' (lease_seconds) - a slow live run and a dead one look the same, and it never reads /proc or boot_id. schedule.py already judges its own children right (state.json pid + boot_id, `gone()`), but only for children of `actl schedule run` and only when that command is re-run. event.py writes `pid` = the pid of the emitting `event.py` process, which is useless for liveness. On the cloud main session, session.start has no session.end (events: 1 start, 0 end), so heartbeat names the live main session as stale after 2 h every time.
hypotheses:
H1 Every start a driver emits can carry the driver's own pid and the boot id (auto-fix.sh / land.sh / review.sh: $$; new-session.sh dispatch: the python wrapper's pid; session-hook.sh: $PPID, best effort). Falsify: find a start path that cannot know its driver pid before emitting - then that path records nothing and its rows stay `unknown`, never `alive`.
H2 'Taken over' is decidable from the event file alone: after a dead start there is a later `ticket.attempt.start` with a higher attempt, or an `agent.start` for the same ticket+role with another run_id, or (land) a later `land.start` whose branches include the same t<n>. Falsify: construct a fixture where the later start belongs to another ticket or the same run_id - it must not count.
H3 A saved `git diff HEAD` plus a clean worktree is enough for the next round: that is exactly what main did by hand for #155, #159, #162, #169 and the next round went on. Falsify: untracked files - `git diff HEAD` misses them, so the diff must be taken after `git add -N .` (intent-to-add) or untracked paths are listed in the diff header; the test fixture has one untracked file.
H4 Liveness needs no signal: /proc/<pid> plus /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id is what schedule.py already uses and hard_block forbids os.kill / killpg / pkill / `kill -` in new test lines anyway.

interface_contracts.events: start kinds gain kv driver_pid=<int> boot_id=<uuid string>; closers added: ticket.attempt.failed kv reason=driver-died; agent.failed kv reason=driver-died; land.fail kv stage=died note=driver-died; session.end kv reason=driver-died. No new kind in event.py KINDS.
interface_contracts.liveness: one function `gone(pid, boot) -> bool` (pid absent from /proc, or boot recorded and != current boot) used by schedule.py and heartbeat; no signals.
interface_contracts.heartbeat_cli: `actl heartbeat [--reconcile]` (scripts/heartbeat.sh; python body may move to scripts/heartbeat.py called by the sh wrapper - actl's table maps heartbeat to the .sh). Verdict words exactly: alive | dead awaiting-takeover | dead taken-over | unknown.
interface_contracts.files: reports/t<n>/<run_id>/wip-round<r>-died.diff (unified diff of `git diff HEAD` after `git add -N .`, taken before cleaning); reports/heartbeat/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.log.
interface_contracts.ticket: only `state` Running->Ready by reconcile (through ticket.py set, state_version +1); cost row through ticket.py cost; nothing else on the ticket.
